question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.


Thousands of people / have died off / the deadly Corona / virus in the world.
options: virus in the world
have died off
Thousands of people
the deadly Corona
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "have died off"

Explanation:
☛ Phrasal Verb Misuse: "Die off" is incorrect here as it implies gradual extinction due to natural causes (e.g., species disappearance).
☛ Contextual Error: For sudden deaths caused by COVID-19, "die" or "die from" is appropriate.
☛ Missing Preposition: "Died off" lacks the required preposition ("from" or "of") to indicate the cause of death.
☛ Exam Tip: Competitive exams frequently test phrasal verb accuracy and preposition omissions in error-spotting questions.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Phrasal Verbs: "Die off" (natural decline) ≠ "Die from" (direct cause).
☛ Prepositions: Use "die of" (disease) or "die from" (external cause) to specify death reasons.
☛ Collocations: "Deadly virus" is correct, whereas "deadly Corona" is incomplete.

Example:
Incorrect - Many birds have died off the flu.
Correct - Many birds have died from the flu.

☛ Contextual Inaccuracy: कोरोना वायरस से अचानक हुई मौतों के लिए "die" या "die from" सही विकल्प हैं।
☛ Preposition Omission: "died off" के बाद "from" या "of" preposition का अभाव है, जो कारण बताने के लिए आवश्यक है।
☛ Exam Focus: प्रतियोगी परीक्षाओं में अक्सर phrasal verbs के गलत प्रयोग और missing prepositions पर प्रश्न पूछे जाते हैं।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Phrasal Verbs: "Die off" vs "Die from" - पहला gradual extinction दर्शाता है, दूसरा direct cause of death।
☛ Prepositions: मृत्यु का कारण बताने के लिए "die of" (बीमारी) या "die from" (बाहरी कारक) का प्रयोग करें।
☛ Collocations: "Deadly virus" सही collocation है, जबकि "deadly Corona" अधूरा प्रयोग है।

Example:
Incorrect - Many birds have died off the flu.
Correct - Many birds have died from the flu.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.


I can clearly / recollect the day / as I first / met you.
options: met you
recollect the day
as I first
I can clearly
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "as I first"

Explanation:
☛ The segment "as I first" is incorrect because 'as' is not suitable here.
☛ The sentence refers to a specific time ("the day"), hence "when" should be used instead.
☛ "As" is generally used for parallel actions, whereas "when" is used for specific time references.
☛ "When" emphasizes a particular moment, which fits the context.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Conjunctions: "When" is used for time-specific events, while "as" indicates simultaneous actions.
☛ Tense Agreement: If the main clause is in Past Tense, the dependent clause must also use Past Tense.

Example:
Incorrect - The day as I first met you was unforgettable.
Correct - The day when I first met you was unforgettable.

☛ वाक्य में "the day" एक विशेष घटना का समय दिखा रहा है, इसलिए "when" का प्रयोग होना चाहिए।
☛ "as" का प्रयोग सामान्यतः दो घटनाओं के समानांतर होने की स्थिति में होता है।
☛ "When" का प्रयोग किसी विशिष्ट समय को दर्शाने के लिए किया जाता है।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Conjunctions (संयोजक): "When" का प्रयोग समय-विशिष्ट घटनाओं के लिए किया जाता है, जबकि "as" का प्रयोग दो घटनाओं के समानांतर होने पर होता है।
☛ Tense Agreement (काल सहमति): यदि मुख्य वाक्य में Past Tense है, तो संबंधित उपवाक्य में भी Past Tense होना चाहिए।

Example:
Incorrect - The day as I first met you was unforgettable.
Correct - The day when I first met you was unforgettable.

question:
In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.


The assistant superintendent stepped down from his duties declaring that the jail was not take care of the inmates.
options: declaring that
of the inmates
stepped down from
was not take care
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "was not take care"

Explanation:
☛ The error lies in the segment "was not take care".
☛ The correct form should be "was not taken care" because "take" must be in its past participle form "taken" in passive voice.
☛ "Take care of" is a phrasal verb meaning "to look after." In passive voice, it becomes "taken care of".
☛ The correct sentence structure should be: "the jail was not taken care of the inmates."

Grammar Rules:
☛ In passive voice, the verb must be in its past participle form (V3).
☛ Phrasal verbs in passive voice retain their prepositions (e.g., "taken care of").
☛ Auxiliary verbs (was/were) are followed by past participles.

Example:
Incorrect - The report was not submit yesterday.
Correct - The report was not submitted yesterday.

☛ यहाँ passive voice का उपयोग होना चाहिए, जहाँ "was not taken care" सही होगा क्योंकि "take" की third form "taken" होती है।
☛ "Take care of" एक phrasal verb है जिसका अर्थ है "देखभाल करना"। Passive voice में इसे "taken care of" लिखा जाता है।

Example:

Correct - The project was not completed on time.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.


He can’t climb this tree, can’t he?
options: No substitution
isn’t it
couldn’t he
can he
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "can he"

Explanation:
☛ This sentence is an example of a Question Tag, which is asked in contrast to the main clause.
☛ The main clause (He can’t climb this tree) is Negative, so the Question Tag should be Affirmative.
☛ After can’t (Negative), can he (Affirmative) is grammatically correct.
☛ Can’t he is incorrect because the Question Tag does not match the Negative form of the main clause.

Grammar Rules:
☛ In Question Tags, the Tense and Auxiliary Verb of the main clause and the tag must agree.
☛ If the main clause is Negative, the tag must be Affirmative, and vice versa.
☛ Modal Auxiliary Verbs (e.g., can, will, should) are repeated in the tag.

Example:
Incorrect - She won’t come tomorrow, won’t she?
Correct - She won’t come tomorrow, will she?

solution_hi:

☛ मुख्य वाक्य (He can’t climb this tree) Negative है, इसलिए Question Tag Affirmative होना चाहिए।
☛ Can’t (Negative) के बाद can he (Affirmative) का प्रयोग सही है।
☛ Can’t he गलत है क्योंकि Question Tag में Negative मुख्य वाक्य के Negative के साथ मेल नहीं खाता।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Question Tags में मुख्य वाक्य और टैग का Tense और Auxiliary Verb समान होना चाहिए।
☛ यदि मुख्य वाक्य Negative है, तो टैग Affirmative होगा और इसके विपरीत।
☛ Modal Auxiliary Verbs (जैसे can, will, should) को टैग में दोहराया जाता है।

Example:
Incorrect - She won’t come tomorrow, won’t she?
Correct - She won’t come tomorrow, will she?

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution required’.


She told you that she is quite afraid of dogs, did she?
options: didn’t she
No substitution required
isn’t she
had she
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "didn’t she"

Explanation:
☛ Here, a Question Tag is used which depends on the main clause.
☛ The main clause "She told you that she is quite afraid of dogs" uses Past Tense (told), so the Question Tag must also be in Past Tense.
☛ Since the main clause is Affirmative, the Question Tag should be Negative.
☛ "didn’t she" is the correct option as it matches the Past Tense (told) and forms a Negative Tag.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Question Tags depend on the Tense and Form (Affirmative/Negative) of the main clause.
☛ If the main clause is Affirmative, the Tag is Negative, and vice-versa.
☛ If the main clause has a Modal Verb (can, could, will, etc.) or Auxiliary Verb (is, am, are, was, were, etc.), the same verb is used in the Tag.
☛ If the main clause has an ordinary verb (e.g., told, went, ate), the Tag uses do/does/did.

Example:
Incorrect - She went to the market, went she?
Correct - She went to the market, didn’t she?

☛ मुख्य क्लॉज "She told you that she is quite afraid of dogs" में Past Tense (told) का प्रयोग हुआ है, इसलिए Question Tag भी Past Tense में होगा।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Question Tag मुख्य क्लॉज के Tense और Form (Affirmative/Negative) पर निर्भर करता है।
☛ यदि मुख्य क्लॉज Affirmative है, तो Tag Negative होगा और vice-versa।
☛ अगर मुख्य क्लॉज में Modal Verb (can, could, will, etc.) या Auxiliary Verb (is, am, are, was, were, etc.) हो, तो Tag में उसी Verb का प्रयोग होगा।
☛ अगर मुख्य क्लॉज में कोई सामान्य Verb (जैसे: told, went, ate) हो, तो Tag में do/does/did का प्रयोग होगा।

Example:
Incorrect - She went to the market, went she?
Correct - She went to the market, didn’t she?

question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.


He didn’t know how getting to the Guest House so he stopped to ask the way.
options: He didn’t know
so he stopped
how getting to
to ask the way
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "how getting to"

Explanation:
☛ "how getting to" is incorrect because the Gerund (getting) is inappropriate here.
☛ It should be replaced with the Infinitive (to get), as "how" requires the base form (to + verb) after it.
☛ Correct Structure: "how + to + verb" (e.g., how to reach, how to solve).
☛ Here, "how to get to" is the correct phrase, as it indicates direction/method.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Infinitive (to + verb) is used after question words (what, how, where) to show method/purpose.
☛ Gerund (-ing form) is used as a noun or after prepositions, not after question words.
☛ In Error Spotting, focus on parallel structure and verb forms.

Example:
Incorrect - He taught me how swimming.
Correct - He taught me how to swim.

☛ इसके बजाय Infinitive (to get) का उपयोग करना चाहिए, क्योंकि "how" के बाद क्रिया के base form (to + verb) का प्रयोग होता है।

Grammar Rules:

question:
In the given sentence, identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.


There is a few water in the bowl on the table.
options: There is
a few water
in the bowl
on the table
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "a few water"

Explanation:
☛ The error lies in "a few water" because "water" is an uncountable noun and cannot be used with "few".
☛ "Few" is used only with countable nouns (e.g., books, pens).
☛ For uncountable nouns (e.g., water, milk), we use "little" or "a little".
☛ Correct sentence: "There is a little water in the bowl on the table."

Grammar Rules:
☛ Countable vs. Uncountable Nouns: Countable nouns (e.g., chairs) can be counted, while uncountable nouns (e.g., sugar) cannot.
☛ Determiners:
- "Few/a few" → Only with countable nouns (few books).
- "Little/a little" → Only with uncountable nouns (little water).
☛ Articles: "A/an" is used only with countable singular nouns (a bowl), not uncountable nouns (❌ a water).

Example:
Incorrect - There is a few sugar in the jar.
Correct - There is a little sugar in the jar.

question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.


I remember to meet her at a conference in Delhi last year.
options: at a conference
I remember
in Delhi last year
to meet her
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "to meet her"

Explanation:
☛ The segment "to meet her" is incorrect because it should be replaced with "meeting her" (gerund form).
☛ When remember is used for a past event, we must use gerund (verb + ing).
☛ Remember + infinitive (to + verb) is used for future actions (something you need to do).
☛ Since the sentence mentions "last year" (a past event), "meeting" is the correct form.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Gerund (verb + ing) is used for past experiences or memories.
☛ Infinitive (to + verb) is used for future intentions or obligations.
☛ Verbs like remember, forget, stop, try change meaning based on whether they are followed by a gerund or infinitive.

Example:
Incorrect - I remember to meet her at a conference in Delhi last year.
Correct - I remember meeting her at a conference in Delhi last year.

Explanation:

☛ Remember के बाद अगर हम किसी past event (पिछली घटना) के बारे में बात कर रहे हैं, तो हमें "meeting" (gerund) का प्रयोग करना चाहिए।
☛ Remember के बाद infinitive (to + verb) का प्रयोग तब होता है जब हम future action (भविष्य की क्रिया) के बारे में बात करते हैं।
☛ यहाँ वाक्य में "last year" (पिछले साल) का उल्लेख है, जो एक past event को दर्शाता है, इसलिए "meeting" सही है।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Gerund (verb + ing) का प्रयोग past events या experiences के साथ किया जाता है।
☛ Infinitive (to + verb) का प्रयोग future actions या intentions के साथ किया जाता है।
☛ Remember, forget, stop, try जैसे verbs के बाद gerund और infinitive का प्रयोग अलग-अलग meanings देता है।

Example:
Incorrect - I remember to meet her at a conference in Delhi last year.
Correct - I remember meeting her at a conference in Delhi last year.

question:
In the given sentence, identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.


Many workers move from one state to another and called migrant workers.
options: Many workers
and called migrant workers
move from one state
to another
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "and called migrant workers"

Explanation:
☛ The segment "and called migrant workers" contains a grammatical error.
☛ The error lies in the incorrect use of passive voice. The intended meaning is: "Many workers move from one state to another and are called migrant workers."
☛ The correct structure requires the auxiliary verb 'are' to form the passive voice ("are called").
☛ In active voice, the sentence would be: "People call them migrant workers.", but in passive, it must be "They are called migrant workers."

Grammar Rules:
☛ In passive voice, the object becomes the subject, and an auxiliary verb (is/am/are/was/were) is used.
☛ For example, the active sentence "They respect him." becomes "He is respected." in passive.
☛ With modal verbs (can, may, must), use be + V3, e.g., "This work must be finished."

Example:
Incorrect - "The book kept on the table."
Correct - "The book is kept on the table."

Grammar Rules:

☛ यदि active voice में वाक्य "They call him a leader." है, तो passive में "He is called a leader." होगा।

question:

options: I am
the crowded city

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "drive on"

☛ The segment "drive on" is incorrect because after "used to", we use a gerund (verb + ing), not the base form of the verb.

☛ Correct structure: getting used to + driving (gerund).
☛ The preposition "to" here requires a gerund, not an infinitive.

☛ Gerund vs. Infinitive: Certain verbs/phrases (e.g., used to, look forward to) always take a gerund after them.
☛ Phrasal Verbs: In phrases like get used to, "to" is a preposition, so it must be followed by a noun/gerund.
☛ Error Spotting Tip: If "to" is followed by a verb, check whether it should be an infinitive or gerund.

Example:
Incorrect - I am getting used to drive on busy roads.
Correct - I am getting used to driving on busy roads.

question:

☛ Correct Subject-Verb order is crucial in English grammar.


Example:

Correct - Which color do you prefer?

question:

options: me a book
which I returned
last week

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "She has given"

Explanation:
☛ The given sentence mentions last week, which is a definite past time reference.
☛ Present Perfect Tense (has given) is used for actions whose time is not specified or which are connected to the present.
☛ Here, Simple Past Tense (gave) should be used because the action occurred at a specific past time (last week).
☛ which I returned is grammatically correct as it appropriately uses the Past Simple Tense.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Present Perfect Tense (has/have + V3) is used for indefinite time. Example: She has visited Paris. (no time mentioned)
☛ Simple Past Tense (V2) is used with definite time expressions. Example: She visited Paris last year.
☛ With time expressions like yesterday, last week, in 2020, etc., we always use Simple Past Tense.
☛ If a sentence has two past actions, both should be in Simple Past Tense when time is specified.

Example:
Incorrect - She has completed her homework yesterday.
Correct - She completed her homework yesterday.

→ "She didn’t took" (Wrong) → "She didn’t take" (Correct).
